promptSet.base:
Use case: identity-preserve
Asset: a production pixel-art game animation sprite atlas, exactly FOUR columns by FOUR rows, sixteen equal square cells in reading order, no gaps, gutters, borders, labels or outside margins. Output one square 1024x1024 image. Each frame represents 125 ms: EIGHT FPS for TWO seconds.
Input 1 is the ORIGINAL portrait and the sole authoritative identity and art reference. Preserve it EXTREMELY CLOSELY, like a careful pixel editor animating a copy of that exact avatar. Keep its head outline, size, placement, angle, proportions, hair, features, colors, clothing, and pixel clusters. Do not beautify, age, de-age, smooth, simplify, narrow, widen, rotate, skew, or reinterpret the face. Preserve the source smile exactly; facial motion is limited to a small blink/wink made by changing eyelid pixels. Keep glasses stationary if present. Do not make a new character design.
If input 2 is supplied, it is ONLY a layout and motion-timing guide, not an identity reference. Do NOT copy its person's face, beard, hair, skin, jacket, body proportions or colors. All appearance must come from input 1.
In every cell, the COMPLETE portrait is centered at the same relative scale and crop as input 1. All head geometry and position stay fixed; shoulder movement is at most 1-2 original pixels. The finished animation displays the entire frame; no static overlay or internal clipping is used. Hands/cards must be whole wherever they overlap the body. Keep gestures near the lower CENTER of the frame, below the chin, inside a centered circular crop. Never cross a cell boundary. Frames 1 and 16 return to the source neutral pose.
Background: single flat neutral PURE WHITE #FFFFFF, like the reference. NO cream, ivory, gray, colored tint, gradients, shadow, background texture, checkerboard, transparency or scenery. Preserve clean crisp pixel art at the original level of detail, readable at 64x64.

sequences.turn: Subtle idle breathing plus one natural blink: frames 1-4 very small shoulder lift; frame 5 eyelids halfway closed; frames 6-7 fully closed; frame 8 eyes reopen; frames 9-15 shoulders settle; frame 16 neutral to loop into frame 1. Nothing is held in the hands. Do not bob, tilt, shrink or move the head.
sequences.lay-down: A restrained three-card-fan celebration. Frame 1 source neutral; frame 2 hand starts to enter lower center; 3 hand rises; 4 one card visible; 5 two cards visible; 6 fan opens; 7 three cards rise to chest; 8 fan reaches just below chin; 9-10 hold the complete fan (white cards, heart/spade/diamond), with a tiny blink; 11 eyes reopen and fan starts lowering; 12-14 progressively lower; 15 hand leaves view; 16 source neutral. Keep all cards visible and whole, never sliced across the face/chest. Original smile remains unchanged.
sequences.lay-off: A modest thumbs-up: frame 1 source neutral; 2-4 hand rises from lower center; 5-7 thumb gently extends at chest height; 8-10 hold a small thumbs-up and make one tiny wink, changing one eyelid only; 11 eye reopens; 12-14 progressively lower hand; 15 hand leaves view; 16 source neutral. Keep the hand appropriately sized and the original expression/head unchanged.

identities.curt: Curt is the exact older man in input 1: short side-parted gray hair, dark rectangular glasses, gray stubble and beard, friendly toothy smile, navy athletic zip jacket with its existing white shoulder stripes. Keep the original slight three-quarter pose, age, eyewear, existing jacket markings, and facial proportions.
identities.kate: Kate is the exact woman in input 1: straight medium-brown hair and bangs, pale blue-gray rectangular glasses, broad friendly smile, black puffer jacket over a gray hoodie. Keep the precise original face shape, hair length/fringe, glasses, age and clothing.
identities.natalie: Natalie is the exact woman in input 1: long blonde hair draped down one side, open friendly smile, green jacket with a brown collar and black/cream striped shirt. Preserve the source's exact hair silhouette, asymmetric hair drape, head shape and smile.
identities.carter: Carter is the exact toddler boy in input 1: backward black cap, little tuft of blonde hair, rosy cheeks, happy small open mouth, red bib overalls over a light-blue shirt with dark-blue sleeve ends. Preserve his young age, original baby face, small body and original detailed pixel-art style. Gesture hands must be small toddler hands. Never give him an adult body, adult hand, beard, mature face, or different hat/clothes.
identities.hannah: Hannah is the exact woman in input 1: long straight honey-blonde hair, round tortoiseshell glasses, slight warm smile with closed lips, light-gray shirt and her existing necklace. Preserve the exact head angle, original soft facial features, glasses shape and detailed pixel-art style. Do not turn her round glasses into rectangular glasses.
identities.maggie-theo: The TWO golden retrievers in input 1 are ONE shared avatar. Keep BOTH dogs in EVERY cell, with exactly the same relative size, face shape, placement and overlap: larger pale-gold dog in front at left and darker-gold dog behind at right wearing its red/plaid bandana. Preserve both muzzles, eyes, nose, ears, fur outlines, bandana, original detailed pixel-art style, and the source framing. No human faces, fingers, hands, arms, clothing or thumbs. Never merge the dogs, exchange their positions, change their breeds, or introduce another animal.

dogSequences.turn: Both dogs remain in their original pose. Use a tiny chest breathing motion, at most one original pixel, and alternating natural blinks: front-left dog half-closes eyes in frame 5, closes in 6, reopens in 7; rear-right dog half-closes in frame 9, closes in 10, reopens in 11. Frames 1-4 and 12-16 have open eyes. Heads do not bob, tilt or move. No hands, paws, cards or extra props enter the frame.
dogSequences.lay-down: Both dogs remain in the original arrangement. A small front paw of the foreground left dog brings a fan of three white playing cards (heart, spade, diamond) into the lower CENTER of the portrait, below both muzzles: frame 1 original, 2-4 paw and cards enter, 5-7 fan opens and rises slightly, 8-10 small proud hold and a blink by the left dog, 11-14 cards lower, 15 paw/card fan leaves, 16 exact original. Show a natural furry DOG PAW touching/supporting the cards, never human fingers. Keep both heads and faces fixed, all cards whole, and the right dog's bandana visible.
dogSequences.lay-off: A small friendly front-paw wave from the foreground left dog. Both dogs keep their original placement and head shapes. Frame 1 original; 2-5 one furry front paw slowly rises at the lower center, well below the muzzle; 6-10 a tiny paw wave, with a blink from the rear-right dog; 11-14 paw lowers; 15 almost neutral; 16 exact original. Paw remains a dog paw without fingers or thumbs. No human gesture/anatomy, no cards. Keep the movement subtle and both dogs visible.
